mathematics.independent_solution: Pre-key visible assessment SHA 58ff4948887b9471b8d975c9f2e40d8016831f119bbe0b8e57d0e7325172c88d independently selected a,c,f,h. O is curvature center, not focus or lens optical center. P's local normal is OP. Focus/parallel correspondences are within the explicit paraxial model, while normal retracing is local exact reflection. Off-axis condition excludes normal axial coincidence in the false alternatives.

option_checks.evidence: Focus-directed paraxial incidence reflects axis-parallel by the reversible focus construction.
A curvature-center line is the local normal and retraces; from the off-axis point it is not axis-parallel. Replacing O by F yields the stated misconception, not a second true option.
At reflecting pole P the axis is the local normal, so equal angles give the stated axial symmetry in the construction plane.
An off-axis parallel ray meets away from P and is not normally incident; it reflects toward F. Treating all curved-surface normals as the pole's normal creates this wrong retrace.
Through F is not through O: focus-directed incidence reflects parallel rather than retracing. The misconception incorrectly makes F the curvature center.
Through O follows the local radius/normal. Incidence and reflection angles are zero, giving reverse travel on the same line.
From an off-axis point the ray at P makes a nonzero angle with OP and reflects at that same angle, not along OP. Identifying the normal does not force every reflected ray onto it.
Axis-parallel rays reflect approximately through the real concave focus in this explicitly paraxial model, not an arbitrary-wide-beam exact convergence claim.
